newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Airlines to double capital.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Airlines to double capital.

text.p: Flag carrier Philippine Airlines Inc said on Tuesday its board had approved the doubling of its capital to 20 billion pesos from 10.0 billion pesos to shore up finances and support an aggressive re-fleeting programme.

The airline had last raised its authorised capital stock to 10.0 billion from 5.0 billion pesos in September last year, which paved the way for tobacco and beer tycoon Lucio Tan to take majority control of the airline.
Tan now has a 57 percent stake in the airline from 33.5 percent previously after most other shareholders decided to waive their pre-emptive rights to the last capital increase, a PAL official said.
PAL's huge re-fleeting programme involves the acquisition of 36 new aircraft by the year 2000 and required investments of $4.0 billion.

The airline had scheduled a special stockholders' meeting on February 11 to formalise the re-capitalisation of the airline to 20 billion pesos divided into four billion shares at five pesos per share.

The additional 10 billion pesos in capital is expected to be paid in two equal installments. The first 5.0 billion pesos on or before March 31, 1997 and the next 5.0 billion by next year which will be called as needed by the board, PAL said.
"We need to comply with leverage ratios from financing institutions abroad," the official said.
Minority shareholders, led by Bank of the Philippine Islands, had opposed Tan's efforts to take over the airline, which has been heavily losing money.
Tan is currently embroiled in a lawsuit with the government over tax evasion charges. He was a silent investor in PAL until he became chairman of the airline in 1994.

During the last capital increase, only Tan and international funds belonging to the Aeropartners group and some individual shareholders aligned with the Cumulus group decided to subscribe to their rights offer.
Aeropartners represents investments of the Cojuangco group which have interests in the Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co, while the Cumulus group is linked to the Ayala group of companies.
The government currently has a 23 percent stake in the airline.
The Cumulus/Ayala group has a 5.4 percent stake and the Aeropartners group 4.6 percent directly and a similar stake indirectly. The rest is held by individual shareholders..
In the 1995/96 fiscal year ending March 31, PAL reported a net loss of 2.18 billion pesos against a 1.72 billion peso loss the previous year.
